derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Restated at replacement capex: GSK spent 4,061mm GBP on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 2,628mm GBP of plant depreciation, 1.52% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -2.23% to -2.47%.

column12: JUDGEMENT on the course. The comparator is Varivax, the standalone varicella vaccine this asset is tested against (NCT06806137 compares two VNS doses with two Varivax doses). The April 2026 list (contract to 3/31/2027) reads $191.365 private, per a search summary; the PDF itself was not opened. In GBP, the currency of the book's GSK seeds: $384.23 at 1.327632 = GBP 289.41 (0.00028941 mm GBP). CMS has no usable figure: Proquad Part D 2024 is 38 beneficiaries at $258 (lookup.py demand), and Varivax has no row. The case against, quantified by the second reader: MMRV is about 13% of US first doses and 80% of second doses (Habib et al., Hum Vaccin Immunother 2026, doi:10.1080/21645515.2026.2660525), and GSK has no US MMRV, so a monovalent varicella vaccine sees about 0.87 + 0.20 = 1.07 doses per vaccinated child, $205.56, not two doses at $384.23. The book's MMRVNS seed separately models GSK's share of second doses. In GBP because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $384.23 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) is GBP 289.41

column12: JUDGEMENT on the list edition and the VFC share. The $115.067 first used here is Varivax's CDC price on the Adult Vaccine Price List (contract to 6/30/2026), not the pediatric VFC contract, per a search summary; VFC children are supplied under the pediatric contract. The pediatric pair is consistent with ProQuad's $186.55 against $289.168 on the same list, contract to 3/31/2026, which the MMRVNS seed uses. The 52.2% VFC share is carried from sny_pcv21.csv, whose MMWR 2024;73(33) citation could not be matched: the VFC Vital Signs report (MMWR 2024;73(31):682-685, doi:10.15585/mmwr.mm7331a2) says about 54% of children aged 18 or under were VFC-eligible in 2023 and VFC buys about half of childhood vaccines; at 0.54 the discount is 11.4%. The case against: the April 2026 list (contract to 3/31/2027), per an unconfirmed search summary, reads $158.98 CDC against $191.365 private, which would make it 8.8% off. The VFC share counts eligible children, not doses drawn. Not a CMS anchor, so neither the Part D 0.5 nor the Part B 0.056604 convention applies; this is a published list price with a sourced discount

column12: JUDGEMENT, at a 1.0 multiple and taken as the plateau. Value share of the whole MMR/V pool stands in for course share. The case for more: Priorix competes only with M-M-R II, so its share of that segment is higher; 2025 was its third full year after its 2022 US approval, and US sales rose 54% on FY2024's GBP 39mm. Solved through the curve below as still ramping (s-curve at index 2 is 35.6% of peak), the peak would be 0.114. The case for less: Q4 2025 US sales were GBP 12mm, down 8% on Q4 2024, an annualised GBP 48mm or 3.3% share, which suggests the 2025 measles-year outbreak lifted the earlier quarters; and ProQuad takes about 80% of US second doses (Habib et al. 2026), so a monovalent varicella vaccine competes mainly for first doses
